newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China refinery to issue 500 mln convertible bonds.
newsitem.headline: China refinery to issue 500 mln convertible bonds.

text.p: Chinese oil refinery Maoming Lianhua Co Ltd has applied to issue 500 million convertible bonds for an eventual share listing on the Shenzhen bourse, a company official said on Tuesday.

The company planned to offer all of the bonds, with a par value of 1.00 yuan each, to its staff and to name Shenzhen J&A Securities Co as the chief underwriter, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.

China's top securities watchdog China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) was reviewing Lianhua's application, with the interest rate, offer and conversion price, maturity and timing of the issue not yet fixed, the official said.
The CSRC would not approve the issue until detailed rules governing convertible bond offers had been drafted and enacted, an official with J&A said.
China announced in April a convertible bond quota worth four billion yuan worth, which would only be granted to some of the nation's top 500 state-run but non-listed enterprises.
Beijing has said each convertible bond offer must be worth a minimum of 100 million yuan and the bonds must have a term of no less than three years and no more than five years.
More than 100 companies have applied to issue the bonds but only a small portion of them would be given approval, industry sources have said.
They have also said they expect several convertible bond issues to be launched by the end of this year.
Lianhua, based in Maoming city in southern Guangdong province, planned to invest the bond proceeds in the construction of a 300,000-tonne ethylene project, the Lianhua official said.

Lianhua's convertible bond offer was backed by the China National Petrochemical Corporation (CNPC), which controlled Lianhua through its 100 percent-owned subsidiary, the giant Maoming Petrochemical Co, a CNPC official said.
Maoming Petrochemical is the largest shareholder in the Shenzhen-listed Maoming Petrochemical Shihua Co Ltd.
Lianhua expects its annual crude oil refining capacity to rise to 8.5 million tonnes in 1997 from 7.2 million tonnes in 199 6, the Lianhua official said.
